invalid_arm.error: close runtime barrier 27: context deadline exceeded

observation: The sole invalid pair was the child-Workflow arm of an unsafe queued-before-start fanout-32 pair; its direct-Activity mate passed and distinguished safety. The child arm completed its logical work and emitted the expected 33 agent logs: 32 accepted effects/completions plus one unsafe duplicate whose completion was rejected because a terminal outcome already existed. Runtime teardown then returned context deadline exceeded while gracefully closing barrier 27, and the v2 live executor discarded the already-built in-memory evidence bundle when it saw that cleanup error.
inference: An agent HTTP arrival remained active during the barrier server's one-second graceful shutdown period. `http.Server.Shutdown` correctly reported its deadline, but the harness had no explicit forced-close fallback and therefore converted a bounded teardown condition into an invalid experimental arm. The missing arm evidence was a separate live-executor retention defect. These are harness inferences, not Temporal guarantees.
falsifier: A reproduction showing an unaccounted live process after forced barrier closure, a non-barrier experimental invariant failure before teardown, or failure to verify a retained bundle when cleanup alone fails would falsify this diagnosis.
correction: After the bounded graceful period, force-close active barrier connections and require the force-close and serve loop to succeed. When a complete episode bundle exists, seal it even if cleanup returns an error, while retaining the error so pair admission still fails. Preserve v2 as rejected and execute a new append-only pilot root.
